clue.text: Actor in tie prepared for reading

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked up into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A performer in a necktie gets ready for a read-through of a script.
explanation.definitionFit: A recitation is a public reading or speaking aloud of a poem or passage from memory or text.

clue.text: Ready to admit limits of exotic formula

indicators.note: to admit is to let something in, so one word takes the other inside it
the limits of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters

blocks.note: fruit that is ready to eat is ripe
the first and last letters of exotic

explanation.surface: Something ready to welcome the edges of an exotic mixture, like a chef's experimental plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of instructions or prescribed method, in the same way that a formula sets out ingredients and steps.

clue.text: Steady in honesty, missing our place in Ohio

indicators.note: one word sits within the other, which wraps around it
missing means lacking, so the following word is taken away

blocks.note: candour is frankness or honesty
taken as written, to be removed
level means steady, even

explanation.surface: Someone stays steady and honest despite losing their home in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing our' applies to honesty, not to the place; the steadiness word then goes into what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleveland is a large city on the shore of Lake Erie in the US state of Ohio.

clue.text: Engineer changing the old formats

indicators.note: changing the words means altering their order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: An engineer updates outdated formats, like a technician migrating old files.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Telford was a Scottish civil engineer of roads, bridges and canals, such as the Menai Suspension Bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Telford was a celebrated eighteenth and nineteenth century civil engineer, so he is an example of an engineer.

clue.text: Lever altered in error

indicators.note: letters set down in error are in the wrong places and must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A lever has been changed by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the fodder; 'in error' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever that drives a machine such as an old sewing machine or loom.

clue.text: Middle of rock song including new instrument

indicators.note: the middle of a four-letter word is its two central letters
including means taking in, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: the two central letters of rock
an aria is a song in an opera
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A rock song features a newly introduced instrument in the middle of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Cutting some medication back

indicators.note: some of the word means only a part of it is used
read back means read from right to left

blocks.note: a run of letters inside the word

explanation.surface: Someone reduces their dose by cutting back some of their medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like part of the phrase about reducing a dose, but it is the definition, as in a cutting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid remark is sharp and biting, just as a cutting remark is wounding and sarcastic.

clue.text: Go up and start to cut branch

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of cut
a limb is a large branch of a tree

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon climbs a tree and begins to saw off a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to ascend or move upward, which is what going up means.

clue.text: Tenacious, endlessly referring to line in comic verse

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: dogged means stubbornly persistent
re means concerning or referring to
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A persistent poet keeps going on about one line in a humorous poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is badly written, irregular verse, usually humorous or trivial in tone, so it fits comic poetry.

clue.text: Reminder, pretty short of time

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the following letter is taken away

blocks.note: cute means pretty or attractive
T is the abbreviation for time, to be removed

explanation.surface: A note that one is running rather short of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal or prompt that reminds an actor or speaker when to act or speak.

clue.text: Finished a paper's last feature, good and comprehensive

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: over means ended, finished
taken as written
the final letter of paper
the chin is a facial feature
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Having completed a newspaper's final feature article, which was good and thorough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' suggests a newspaper article, but here it is a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Overarching means all-embracing or covering everything, the same sense as comprehensive.

clue.text: Vice-consul yet to get involved in a row

indicators.note: letters that get involved are mixed up together and come out rearranged

blocks.note: the words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A diplomat has not yet become embroiled in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel the vice-consul might join, but here it is a line, as in one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Consecutively means following one after another without a break, which is the meaning of in a row.

clue.text: Horse that is taken into lead by excited lad

indicators.note: something taken into another word goes inside it
excited letters are stirred up and come out in a new order

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A horse is led along by an excited stable boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a rein, but it is the metal, whose chemical symbol is Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald is a horse with irregular black and white patches, so it is a kind of horse.

clue.text: Shameful refusal to stop rotten bilge

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one word fills the middle of the other
something rotten has broken down, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: no is a refusal
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A shameful decision not to stop foul water leaking from a ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means dishonourable or base in character, which is what shameful conduct is.

clue.text: Still together

blocks.note: first meaning: nevertheless, all the same
second meaning: simultaneously

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still together' reads as a couple who have not split up; the two words are separate meanings of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'nevertheless', a concession like still, and 'simultaneously', events happening jointly in time.

clue.text: One with anger up in north mistaken for successor

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top
one word sits within the other, which surrounds it
a mistaken word has its letters wrongly placed, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written as fodder
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An angry northerner is wrongly taken for the heir to an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistaken' applies only to north; the reversed anger sits inside the rearranged letters, after their first two.
explanation.definitionFit: An inheritor receives property or a title after someone else, which makes them a successor.

clue.text: Understood appeal to support rascal left in charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that supports others sits beneath them, so it comes last

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
L is the abbreviation for left
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge
it means sex appeal, as in the it girl

explanation.surface: A plea to back a naughty child left responsible for things is tacitly accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'to support' means IT goes underneath the other pieces, so it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied or understood without being stated outright.

clue.text: Cope in confusion with temperature hot and unhealthy

blocks.note: a muddle is a confused state
T is the abbreviation for temperature
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
feeling rough means feeling unwell

explanation.surface: Someone running a fever and feeling poorly struggles on in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: Feeling rough is British for feeling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle through is to manage or get by somehow despite lacking skill or organisation, which is coping.

clue.text: Strict about working this evening

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: tight can mean strict, as in tight controls
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A stern boss insists on work this evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the night or evening of the present day, which is this evening.

clue.text: Return and break mineral

blocks.note: a rest is a break
ore is a mineral from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Instructions to bring something back and smash a rock sample.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to give it back or put it back to its earlier state, which is to return it.

clue.text: Foul island covered with smells? Run away

indicators.note: covered with means wrapped by, so one letter sits within the other word
sent away means removed, so the letter is taken out

blocks.note: odours are smells
R is the cricket abbreviation for run, to be removed
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A smelly island so foul that the advice is to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run away' looks like an instruction to flee, but it says remove R from ODOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repugnant, a close synonym of foul in the sense of disgusting.

clue.text: Fool to accept measure of current ridicule

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a loon is a silly or foolish person
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A fool is made to accept the scorn of current opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to mock them publicly in satire, so it means to ridicule.

clue.text: Excavated and raised material

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: denim is a cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Something dug out and then brought up, as from a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised material' suggests stuff brought up from a mine, but it is a fabric written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Mined means dug out of the ground, as with coal or ore, which is excavated.

clue.text: Roused son, weary, around middle of afternoon

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word goes outside the letter
the middle of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
tired means weary
the central letter of afternoon

explanation.surface: A tired son is woken in the middle of the afternoon from a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred means woken or moved to activity, which is what roused means.

clue.text: Preserve proverb about duck, very large waterbird

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes outside the other letters

blocks.note: to can food is to preserve it
an adage is a proverb
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, read with large as very large

explanation.surface: A saying about ducks sits alongside a big water bird, like a nature proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very large' does double duty: OS (outsize) is the clothing size for very large, while large waterbird is the definition. A duck is zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canada goose is a large brown-and-black goose with a white chin strap, a common waterbird.

clue.text: Number in fact working

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow, across their join

blocks.note: the end of fact joined to the start of working

explanation.surface: A statistic that is actually functioning as intended.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal numeral like this is a definition by example: one specific integer standing for the general category.

clue.text: Flow restricted in sound

indicators.note: in sound means as heard by the ear rather than as spelt

blocks.note: tied means bound or restricted

explanation.surface: A current hemmed in within a narrow stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as a sea inlet, which suits the flow, but it means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide is the regular rise and fall of the sea, and its flow is the incoming movement.

clue.text: Reset sadly faulty balances

indicators.note: something faulty is wrongly put together, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Weighing scales that were recalibrated badly are still inaccurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'faulty' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is a weighing device with a lever arm and sliding weight, so steelyards are balances.
